header.question:
A document in the library contains this sentence:

> Using individual neurons as these units has had some success (Olah et al., 2020; Bills et al., 2023), but a key challenge has been that neurons are almost always polysemantic, with nearly every neuron activating for several unrelated types of feature (Olah et al., 2020).

Check what the sentence says about the work it cites against that work in the library. Does the cited source support it? Cite the page(s) of the cited source that show what it actually says.

args.text:
Verdict: not supported

The cited Olah et al. source supports the narrower point that polysemantic neurons occur: it says neural networks “often contain” such neurons and gives one InceptionV1 neuron responding to cat faces, car fronts, and cat legs. It also says polysemantic neurons are a major challenge. That does not support the sentence’s stronger quantifier “almost always” or the claim that nearly every neuron activates for several unrelated feature types. [distill:zoom-in/r1/b62] [distill:zoom-in/r1/b65]

Olah et al. also present examples of studying individual features/neurons, including curve detectors and a pose-invariant dog head detector, so the broad claim of some success is consistent with the source. [distill:zoom-in/r1/b26] [distill:zoom-in/r1/b55]

events.delta:
Verdict: not supported

Olah et al. support the narrower claim that polysemantic neurons are a challenge: they say neural networks “often contain” neurons that respond to multiple unrelated inputs, and give an example of one neuron responding to cat faces, car fronts, and cat legs. They call polysemantic neurons a major challenge for understanding networks. Those passages do not support the stronger “almost always” / “nearly every neuron” wording. [distill:zoom-in/r1/b62] [distill:zoom-in/r1/b65]

The “some success” characterization is consistent with Olah et al.’s examples of studying curve detecting neurons and a pose invariant dog head detector. [distill:zoom-in/r1/b27] [distill:zoom-in/r1/b55]
